 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 08.06.2011 in MVC.No.224/2005 passed by the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Ramanagaram, for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

sentences.text: 2. The factum of accident is not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

As per the medical evidence on record including the evidence of doctors-P.W.2 and P.W.3, the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
a) Head Injury with diffuse axonal injury and fracture let frontal orbit root left temporal contusion.

sentences.text: 5. The above said injuries are grievous in nature.
The claimant had suffered loss of sensation in right hand and also suffered right famur.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries sustained, the compensation of Rs.30,000/- awarded under the head injury, pain and suffering is on the lesser side.
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the injury, pain and suffering.
6. The Tribunal has committed error in awarding compensation of Rs.1,61,571/- under the head medical expenses compared to the medical bills produced before the Tribunal.
The claimant has produced the medical bills worth Rs.1,83,526/-, but the Tribunal has wrongly deducted Rs.21,955/-.

Therefore, this Court without seeing any double claim and duplication of medical bills, accordingly,
compensation of Rs.1,84,000/- is awarded under the head medical expenses.

7. The doctor-P.W.2 had assessed the physical disability at 10% towards the head injury, 15%
towards right hand and 20% towards right leg and assessed the whole body disability at 15%.
P.W.3 is another doctor who had stated that the claimant had suffered 20% of permanent physical disability towards the whole body.
The Tribunal has committed error in taking only 15% as disability.
The Tribunal has not stated as to whether it can be held as physical disability or functional disability.
Physical disability and functional disability are two different aspects.
In this regard, this Court places reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another 1.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimant is stated to be working as a mechanic in garage.
It is reflected in the complaint lodged before the police and also he has stated in his evidence that for the work of mechanic in garage documentary evidence cannot be expected.
Therefore, on all its preponderance of probabilities, the profession of the claimant is considered as a mechanic in garage.
The nature of injuries sustained by the claimant resulting into losing sensation to the right hand and right leg femur fracture, certainly, it affects the earning capacity of the claimant.
The work of mechanic requires skill through hands and involves physical work.
Therefore, when the claimant had sustained fracture of right hand femur and loss of sensation, the functional disability is found to be significant one.

Therefore, considering the evidence of (2011) 1 SCC 343 doctors-P.W.2 and P.W.3 and other evidence on record, it is just and proper to take 25% as functional disability by following the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar's case.
8. The accident was caused on 02.05.2005.
Therefore, notional income ought to be taken as Rs.4,000/- per month.

Since the claimant had sustained grievous injuries as above stated,
substantially it affects his earning capacity as a mechanic.
Therefore, it affects the loss of future income also.

Therefore, as per the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar2, additional income is to be added towards future prospects in life.
